issues.problem: The compiled selector decomposes the intended single conjunctive condition ('the same channel is both the Robert-named user's CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP and an on-call/incident-topic channel') into two independent existentials: a focal path (teams→user_teams→users→channel_members, filtered on display_name='Robert') and an auxiliary path (teams→channels, filtered on topic containing 'on-call') that shares only the team_id, not the specific channel_id from the focal path. This means the query does not actually enforce that the qualifying Robert's channel membership is in the on-call channel — it only enforces that the workspace independently contains *some* Robert with *some* channel membership and *some* on-call-topic channel, which happen to coincide in this seed but are not joined as the same channel. The binding_note and prompt explicitly require the same-channel relationship ('also belongs to the on-call ... channel there'), so this is a construction fidelity gap even though the current seed data (only one relevant channel per team) avoids producing an incorrect result.
issues.repair: Rewrite the selector as a single path teams→user_teams→users→channel_members→channels with the topic filter applied on the channels node reached via channel_members.channel_id (i.e., filter on the same channel row the user belongs to), removing the disjoint auxiliary existential, so the join structure matches the intended relationship rather than relying on seed-specific coincidence.

rationale: The route WORKSPACE→WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP→USER→CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP is exercised correctly at the seed level: T01WORKSPACE (via pre-existing Robert Chen plus newly added Robert Walsh membership in C_INFRA, whose topic explicitly mentions on-call/incidents) and the newly constructed T02VELOCITY (Robert Kim in C_ONCALL, topic/purpose explicitly about on-call/incident response) both genuinely satisfy the full chain, producing the intended two-way ambiguity consistent with the declared underspecified resolution_mode and the binding_note's explicit acknowledgment. The negatives are well-differentiated and non-redundant: T03GAMMA isolates the channel-topic condition, T04DELTA (Roberta Nguyen) isolates the exact first-name match, and Robert Fields (message author without channel_members row in C_INFRA) correctly tests that message authorship cannot substitute for CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP — exactly the distinction the review criteria call out. mechanical_checks show computed_matches == expected_matches and computed_focal_negatives correctly excludes T04DELTA, with no reported errors. Answer-computation attributes (teams.team_name, teams.team_id) are bare columns matching the requested 'name and ID.' Actor was granted workspace membership in all candidate/negative workspaces, consistent with a plausible discovery-based access_plan using documented users.list/conversations.members/conversations.info calls, and no disallowed field (timestamps, edit history, etc.) is requested. The one substantive concern is that the compiled selector's auxiliary existential is not properly joined to the focal channel_members row, so the 'same channel' requirement central to the prompt and binding_note is not strictly encoded in the query construction, even though it does not currently cause an incorrect result given the seed's channel distribution. This is a construction-quality flaw rather than an outcome-affecting validity failure, so validity passes but quality is capped at adequate.
